interpretation: V144 may forecast aggregate next-session risk only. Leader selection probability cannot be claimed improved until V150 specific-theme factors pass a new isolated group walk-forward and complete-trade validation. V161 permits severe-abnormal rule-distance diagnostics only, not a calibrated hit probability or buy ranking. V162/V163 do not authorize a two-to-three-day emotion probability; daily output must remain main/alternative/risk scenarios with invalidation conditions. V164 keeps theme membership separate from catalyst timing and expectation saturation; current theme evidence cannot train or rerank candidates. V158/V194/V195/V197/V198/V199/V200/V201/V202/V203 now govern 74 short-term hypotheses; all remain research-only until isolated out-of-sample tests pass. V194 corrects the fast-board execution denominator and separates observable thin/one-price structure from unobservable control intent; neither fast structure nor alleged control may rank a stock or authorize entry. V195 proves that sparse review dates cannot define the trading calendar: the 2026-09-01 label previously skipped the actual 09-02 and 09-03 sessions. V124-V126, V160, V167 and V194 are rebuilt on the verified calendar, and a missing immediate pool now stays unavailable rather than moving forward. V196 targets executable B+2 profit and B+1 tail loss separately from promotion. Its ten complete evaluation sessions show only a diagnostic 40% top-one B+2-positive rate for the emotion model, with negative mean B+2 return and 30% B+1 large-loss rate; no ranking or entry is authorized. V197 then joins the profit sample to the point-in-time theme archive. Only 56 of 456 evaluation rows on four of ten sessions have a pre-open roster, no row has a complete driver-and-expectation schema, and the covered group does not outperform unknown names. Roster availability is attention/coverage evidence, not a theme-strength or entry factor. V198 shows why the 40% emotion top-one hit rate is still unusable: average B+2 return is -3.77%, payoff ratio 0.66, profit factor 0.44 and the full-capital path drawdown proxy is about 47.81%. Win rate, payoff magnitude and tail risk remain separate gates. V199 then builds the tail gate as a separate prequential rejector. Its best candidate-level AUC is only 0.576, the descriptive highest-risk quintile does not concentrate large losses, and fixed thresholds that temporarily retain zero large losses keep only two or three losing trades. Multiplying profit and risk probabilities also worsens both mean payoff and tail loss; no risk model, veto threshold, position sizing rule or entry is authorized. V200 separates the opening call-auction result from the later continuous-auction decision. Five-to-seven and above-seven percent opening groups show about 25% descriptive large-loss rates in the recent first-board sample, but the three frozen top-one large losses span both negative and positive opening gaps. The matched opening result cannot filter a fill at that same auction price; 09:30/09:35 use requires a new execution price, minute evidence and labels, while current complete intraday sequences remain zero. V201 then enforces T+1 exit realism: B-session drawdown thresholds are not executable stops, B+1 one-price lower limits are unsellable, and other lower-limit opening queues remain fill-unverifiable. Tail protection must act before entry through abstention and position limits; no fixed-stop guarantee or entry is authorized. V202 applies the same-event rule to exits. The official open may proxy only a precommitted auction exit; an open-conditioned sale needs a later price, and ex-post choice between open and close is a prohibited timing oracle. No historical broker exit, post-open exit model, or timing policy is promoted. V203 separates broad-index direction from the board-relay ecology. Index-up with non-positive prior-limit median feedback shows a descriptive next-adverse-rate gap, but discovery and validation intervals cross zero, the validation divergence group has only fourteen sessions, and every replication gate fails. The layer may be shown as context but cannot override short-term losses, gate emotion, rerank stocks, or authorize entry. V166 does not authorize relay cumulative turnover as a ranking factor. V167 does not authorize failed-seal path as a positive ranking factor. V168 prevents secondary theme rosters from being promoted to verified catalyst or high-low evidence. V169 separately verifies business membership, active driver and expectation; verified membership alone remains descriptive and cannot authorize ranking or high-low mapping. V170 keeps first-board and relay cross-theme races in separate lanes and uses same-confidence peers only; current incomplete scope authorizes neither training, winner selection nor entry. V171 separates arithmetic threshold proximity from a fully evidenced path role; the current full-pool replay has zero verified candidate distances and therefore selects neither a closest candidate nor a path-potential candidate. V172 finds a descriptive promotion premium for two-level-or-greater ladder gaps, but middle-damage separation and conditional B+2 evidence are unstable; ladder gaps remain identity context rather than a positive ranking factor. V173 finds that the first turnover board after a one-price streak retains next-day identity premium, but it does not establish a B+2 payoff edge or monotonic benefit from higher turnover; first opening remains delayed-price-discovery risk requiring intraday and theme confirmation. V174 makes all six roles and both group-primary lanes explicit; absent validated evidence, the unique comprehensive result is cash, and the contract itself never authorizes entry. V175 rejects an any-low-stock promotion flag as nearly constant and uses realized lane promotion-rate dominance only for scenario review; it cannot be leaked into the prior close or authorize a high-to-low trade. V176 corrects Level-1 auction semantics and freezes a minute propagation-order contract, but no real forward observations exist; neither net matched-amount change nor event order proves cancellation intent, causal feedback, stock ranking, or entry. V177 separates broad from narrow profit distribution: a positive mean with a non-positive median cannot upgrade the environment by itself. Its aggregate historical scenario is descriptive and cannot rerank stocks or authorize entry. V178 separates clean and fragile breadth expansion; its full-sample and validation directions agree, but discovery and validation intervals do not both pass. It may be displayed as a repair-quality warning, not used as an emotion gate, stock ranker, or entry. V179 finds no monotonic next-session deterioration from aggregate one-price-board share and only eleven formal-consensus sessions. One-price share may describe crowding, delayed price discovery, and buyability, but cannot be a direct emotion gate or entry signal. V180 extends breadth quality to aggregate B+1/B+2/B+3 market paths; recent validation is adverse for fragile expansion, but discovery intervals cross zero. Only an uncalibrated scenario warning is allowed, never a candidate holding-period or entry inference. It cannot enter the prior-close model, and no band can authorize stock reranking or entry without intraday and theme confirmation. V183 conditions the opening-gap tradeoff on supportive, hot, and adverse emotion groups. Payoff effects do not replicate across time segments, so emotion cannot waive the above-7% risk flag, create an automatic veto, rerank stocks, or authorize entry. V184 retains every low-open candidate in the opening denominator. Conditioning on later limit touch inflates the validation B+2-positive rate by about 10.6 times and uses future information; low opens are neither automatic buys nor automatic rejects and require live reclaim, VWAP, volume, and theme confirmation. Promotion probability cannot replace separate buyability, payoff, big-loss, or complete-trade targets. V187 separates a broad repair close from proven next-session follow-through. The recent validation segment is directionally better, but discovery and validation intervals cross zero; repair quality can frame a scenario only and cannot provide a calibrated relapse probability, emotion gate, stock reranking, position, or entry. V188 separates first-board, middle-board, and height-layer repair transmission. Middle confirmation loses its discovery advantage in validation, and only three recent sessions confirm all layers; layer structure cannot become a hard emotion gate, positive stock factor, position-size increase, or entry signal. V189 separates an aggregate healthy high-to-low ecology window from collapse-masked low-layer strength. Recent direction does not replicate in development, and no specific-theme stock identity exists; the window cannot select a supplement, create a same-theme mapping, increase position size, or authorize entry. V190 separates first-board new-cycle attention from relay height attention. High relay share does not stably suppress first-board payoff, while high first-board supply is adverse to relays only in the recent segment. Lane supply is context only: it cannot create a common winner score, replace specific-theme evidence, rerank a stock, or authorize entry. V191 attaches provider-aligned 10/30-session arithmetic to all 80 current closing candidates and matches every provider close to the frozen pool. Exchange-publication resets were initially unreconciled. V192/V193 now verify every official SSE session since the active rule date and remove that blocker for all 32 SSE candidates; CNINFO zero-result searches for 48 SZSE candidates are deliberately not treated as exhaustive exchange evidence.
